headline: PLS surges nearly 5% on lithium optimism while gold hits record highs and GTA 6 leaks keep Take-Two in the headlines.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a strong session today, up nearly 5% to $5.07. The move came on the back of renewed optimism around lithium demand — analysts are pointing to the AI infrastructure boom as a long-term driver for battery metals, with lithium flagged alongside copper and uranium as key beneficiaries. Sentiment in the lithium sector has been shifting more positively.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS slipped 1.3% today to $528.00. This ASX-listed ETF tracks the entire US share market, so today's dip reflects some softness being priced in from broader market movements. Note that the US indices actually rose last night — the local VTS price can lag or diverge slightly due to the AUD/USD exchange rate and timing differences.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dipped about 1% today to $16.20 and remains the biggest loss-maker in the portfolio at -14.2% overall. No specific news drove today's move — it's a broad AI-themed ETF and tends to move with global tech sentiment. The long-term AI thematic is still intact, but this one has been under pressure since purchase.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged down 0.48% today to $76.91 — barely a blip for a diversified fund. No specific catalyst; this broadly reflects a slightly softer ASX session today with the ASX 200 down 0.27%.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE nudged up 0.24% today to $93.56. Emerging markets got a small tailwind from a stronger Australian dollar (AUD/USD rose 0.78% last night), which affects how this fund is priced locally.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT gained 0.43% last night to $483.24. Analysts are increasingly bullish — one forecast has MSFT potentially breaking $570 as Azure cloud revenue growth holds at 40% year-on-year. Strong AI-driven earnings continue to underpin the stock.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG rose 1.05% last night to $341.75, continuing a solid run. No specific news catalyst, but the broader AI optimism and strong tech sector sentiment is keeping Alphabet well supported.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO slipped just 0.22% last night to $239.62 — essentially flat despite the GTA 6 leak saga entering its fourth day. Take-Two has been subpoenaing Microsoft and Discord to track down the source of leaked gameplay videos. Markets seem to be taking the leaks in stride for now, viewing them as a blip rather than a structural problem.

watch_today.title: PLS surge — a turning point or a bounce?
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped nearly 5% today to $5.07, its best session in a while. Analysts are citing the AI infrastructure boom as a long-term driver for lithium demand. You're still down 24.8% overall on this position, so it's a long road back — but the direction today is encouraging. For a long-term holder, sit tight and let this thesis play out.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 leaks: noise or real risk for TTWO?
watch_today.detail: GTA 6 leaked gameplay videos have been spreading for four days running and Take-Two has now subpoenaed both Microsoft and Discord to find the source. Markets barely flinched — TTWO dropped just 0.22% last night. BBC analysis suggests it's likely a blip, not a disaster, for the biggest game of the year. Long-term thesis (GTA 6 launch) is still intact. Hold.

watch_today.title: GXAI still underwater — but the AI thematic isn't going away
watch_today.detail: GXAI.AX dipped another 1% today and sits at a 14.2% loss overall. There's no specific bad news — it's just been a tough ride for this AI-themed ETF. The global AI story (regulation debates, rising enterprise adoption, new tools) is still very much alive. For a long-term buyer of the AI theme, this is a hold — and potentially worth averaging down if you have appetite.

watch_today.title: Gold hitting record highs — tailwind for broader risk sentiment
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 2.39% last night to USD $4,624 — a remarkable move for the safe-haven metal. This usually signals investors are nervous about something (Middle East tensions, US political uncertainty). Watch whether this spills into broader market caution when US markets open tonight.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Azure growth holding strong, analysts eyeing $570
watch_today.detail: Microsoft closed at $483.24 last night and analysts are flagging Azure cloud revenue growth at 40% year-on-year as the key driver. One forecast has MSFT potentially reaching $570. Nothing to do here — just a reassuring signal that the long-term AI and cloud thesis is playing out.

watch_today.title: Middle East tensions escalating — watch oil and travel stocks
watch_today.detail: Multiple regional airlines including Emirates and Etihad are cancelling flights amid ongoing Middle East tensions. Iran claims its military emerged stronger from recent conflict. Gaza ceasefire talks are reportedly being undermined by fresh Israeli strikes. Oil dipped slightly despite this, but further escalation could push energy prices higher — something to keep an eye on globally.

world.summary: The Middle East remains the biggest global flashpoint, with Iran claiming military strength, Gaza talks stalling, and regional airlines cancelling flights. In the US, the Trump administration's targeting of political opponents and voting rule changes are dominating headlines. Gold is surging to record levels amid global uncertainty.

stories.title: Gaza ceasefire talks undermined by fresh Israeli strikes
stories.why_it_matters: Mediators trying to broker a Gaza ceasefire say the latest Israeli airstrikes are actively undermining negotiations at what they're calling a 'critical stage'. This matters because a broader ceasefire deal would reduce regional instability — and right now the opposite is happening. Each failed negotiation round raises the risk of the conflict widening further into Lebanon, Iran, or beyond, with knock-on effects for global oil prices and financial markets.

stories.title: Iran claims its armed forces emerged stronger from the latest war
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's military is publicly claiming it came out of its most recent conflict stronger — a significant statement that signals Tehran has no intention of backing down diplomatically or militarily. Iran also condemned fresh US economic sanctions as 'economic terrorism'. This combination of defiant rhetoric and new sanctions raises the risk of further escalation in a region already on edge, which can affect global oil supply and trigger safe-haven buying (like the gold surge we saw last night).

stories.title: Middle East flight disruptions: Emirates, Etihad and others cancel flights
stories.why_it_matters: Emirates, Etihad and other major regional airlines are cancelling flights due to ongoing tensions across the Middle East. If you're travelling to or through the region, this is directly relevant — routes through Dubai and Abu Dhabi are being disrupted. More broadly, sustained flight disruptions signal just how serious the security situation has become on the ground and in regional airspace.

stories.title: Trump administration targeted individuals list — including James Comey
stories.why_it_matters: ABC News has published a list of individuals the Trump administration has targeted, including former FBI Director James Comey. This is part of a broader pattern of the administration using government power against perceived political opponents — prosecutors, civil servants, and officials who crossed Trump in his first term. It's raising serious concerns among legal experts about the politicisation of law enforcement in the US, with implications for the rule of law and institutional trust.

stories.title: US Postal Service tightens mail-in voting rules despite court orders
stories.why_it_matters: The US Postal Service has introduced new rules that make mail-in voting harder — this is happening despite federal court orders attempting to block such changes. Mail-in voting became hugely important during COVID and has been a contentious issue since. Restricting it could affect millions of Americans who rely on postal ballots, particularly the elderly and those in rural areas. The fact that this is proceeding despite court orders is itself a significant rule-of-law concern.

politics.summary: Domestic politics is relatively quiet today, with the main story being the federal government striking a deal to fund an ACT gun buyback scheme.

stories.title: Federal government to fund majority of ACT gun buyback scheme
stories.why_it_matters: The federal Labor government has agreed to fund the bulk of a gun buyback program in the ACT (Australian Capital Territory) following negotiations between the two governments. Gun buybacks — where the government purchases firearms from owners to reduce the number in circulation — are periodically used in Australia to tighten gun control. The ACT scheme is relatively small-scale but signals ongoing bipartisan commitment to Australia's strict firearms framework. The federal contribution means ACT residents and taxpayers won't bear the full cost.

ai.summary: Today's AI news is dominated by regulation — from US state laws to financial sector rules to medical devices. There's also a practical money-saving tool worth knowing about if you use multiple AI services.

stories.title: Ramp launches free AI model router that cut client costs by 40%
stories.why_it_matters: Fintech company Ramp has launched a free tool that automatically routes your AI queries to whichever AI model (GPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) can handle them most cheaply — without you having to think about it. Early clients have reportedly cut their AI costs by 40%. For businesses or individuals paying for multiple AI subscriptions, this kind of intelligent routing could become standard practice. It's a sign that the AI market is maturing from 'which model is best' to 'how do we use them efficiently'.

stories.title: FDA asks for public feedback on AI medical device regulation
stories.why_it_matters: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is seeking public input on how to regulate AI-powered medical devices — things like AI diagnostic tools that can read scans, flag cancer, or monitor patients. This is a big deal because AI is increasingly embedded in healthcare, but the rules around how it gets approved and monitored are still being written. The FDA's openness to public feedback suggests they're aware they need to get this right before AI becomes even more central to medical decisions.

stories.title: Finance sector needs its own AI rulebook, new study says
stories.why_it_matters: A new study argues that generic AI laws aren't enough for the financial sector — banks, insurers, and investment platforms need their own dedicated AI rules that account for the specific risks of automated financial decisions (think: AI that denies loans, flags fraud, or manages portfolios). Without tailored regulation, there are real risks of bias, errors, and accountability gaps when AI makes decisions about your money. This is increasingly relevant as more financial products quietly incorporate AI decision-making.

stories.title: Connecticut passes landmark omnibus AI law (SB5) — US states leading the way
stories.why_it_matters: Connecticut has passed one of the most comprehensive state-level AI laws in the US, covering how AI systems must be developed, tested, and governed — particularly when they make decisions affecting people's lives (hiring, lending, healthcare). With the US federal government slow to legislate, individual states like Connecticut are filling the gap. This creates a patchwork of rules that tech companies (including Alphabet and Microsoft, which you hold) will need to navigate across different states — adding compliance costs but also creating clearer rules of the road.

markets.summary: The ASX slipped slightly today, down 0.27% to 9,058. Last night in the US, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ gained 0.43% — modest but positive sessions. Gold was the big mover, surging 2.39% to USD $4,624 amid Middle East tensions. Oil dipped slightly. The Aussie dollar strengthened, up 0.78% to 71.75 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Slight pullback today — broader global caution weighing on the local market.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Modest gains last night — tech and AI stocks leading the way.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: In line with the S&P — AI and big tech holding up well.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Big move — gold surging to record levels as Middle East tensions drive investors to safe havens.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Slight dip despite Middle East tensions — markets not fully pricing in a supply disruption yet.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar strengthening — good for purchasing power, but can reduce the AUD value of US holdings.

sport.summary: It's Super Saturday in the NRL with three games today — Sea Eagles stunned Newcastle 44-24, and the Rabbitohs vs Warriors is live right now in the first half. On the AFL front, Carlton are surging toward ninth spot. NRLW action also underway.

stories.title: Sea Eagles blitz Knights 44-24 in stunning Saturday afternoon win
stories.why_it_matters: Manly Sea Eagles demolished the Newcastle Knights 44-24 at McDonald Jones Stadium in the afternoon game. A sin-bin incident sparked a Manly blitzkrieg that blew the game open — though there was also injury concern for Manly during the match. A massive result that keeps Manly's finals push well alive. Knights' season continues to unravel.

stories.title: Broncos edge Raiders 34-30 in Friday night thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Brisbane Broncos came from behind to beat the Canberra Raiders 34-30 at GIO Stadium on Friday night. A tight contest that went down to the wire — Broncos get the four points and keep their finals position secure. Raiders will be disappointed after holding a lead.

stories.title: Rabbitohs vs Warriors — live in first half, Warriors lead 12-4
stories.why_it_matters: The New Zealand Warriors are leading the South Sydney Rabbitohs 12-4 at half-time at Accor Stadium. Warriors are in strong form and looking to lock up a finals spot. Rabbitohs will need a big second half to get back in this one.

stories.title: Carlton surge toward ninth spot in AFL with big first half lead
stories.why_it_matters: Carlton are building a big lead in their AFL fixture today, pushing hard to grab ninth spot on the ladder. With finals spots still very much up for grabs across the competition, the Blues' form run at this stage of the season could prove decisive in whether they play finals footy this year.
